niche: a Dutch and Flemish audiobook subscription app (four plans: Flex 10 hours, Standaard 30 hours, Onbeperkt, Gezin with up to four profiles) choosing which plan its spring 2027 paid campaign leads with, valued over each sign-up's first 24 months after the publishers' 2027 per-hour remuneration replaces the 2026 revenue share
answer: lead the spring 2027 campaign with Gezin (EUR 22.0 per trial start over 24 months after EUR 0.40 per counted hour and the agency's fee, EUR 8.7 ahead of Flex); not Onbeperkt, which the careful route leads with
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst cleans the exports, reconciles the session log to the publishers' statements and scales its hours up to them in proportion, joins sessions to today's profiles and plans, and values each plan's sign-ups on hours that miss the offline listening the licence renewals alone carry (heaviest on Onbeperkt) and that count Gezin's re-listening across the two channels, so it leads with Onbeperkt.
domain_test: Each result is a subscription cohort quantity the LTV task type estimates (plan-level survival and net revenue per sign-up over 24 months, counted listening per paying subscription-month under the publishers' counting rule, the remuneration it costs), and the counting rule, offline licences, family profiles and per-hour royalties belong to audio subscriptions; swap the nouns into a hospital or a factory and none of the quantities exists.
layer1: session export rows re-sent by the app after a reconnect
profile ids of removed family profiles absent from today's profile table
playback speed recorded per session, content hours against wall time
app-store subscriptions reported in the stores' own monthly proceeds reports
publisher codes renamed in the 2025 catalogue migration
stakeholder_role: the head of growth, who sets the spring 2027 campaign's lead plan with finance

world.org_type: an audiobook and e-book subscription app

driver: The cost of each option's future entrants is a per-unit charge on a quantity the organisation's own counting engine produces from two reporting channels, one of which the main activity record never sees and which is concentrated in some options, under a rule that counts each item once across both channels, so the activity record scaled to the engine's totals misprices the options in opposite directions and the latest cost per entrant reflects a charging basis that ends.
driver_concrete: Each plan's first-24-month contribution per spring 2027 trial start is its net revenue over the plan's spring 2024 trial starts' realised months at 2027 prices less EUR 0.40 per counted hour (the 2027 agreement, replacing 2026's 52 per cent of revenue) and the agency's fee, where counted hours are the furthest position each profile first reaches in each title across the live roll-up and the positions downloaded titles report at licence renewal, attributed to the account whose charge listed the profile that month.
stump: A careful but hurried analyst takes the live roll-up as the listening (it reproduces the 2026 statements exactly) and joins it to today's profile export, which misses Onbeperkt's downloaded listening and credits Gezin with the histories its moved-in profiles brought, and leads with Onbeperkt instead of Gezin; the licence channel alone leads with Standaard.
results: R1 paying subscriptions by plan at 31 Oct 2026; R2 counted hours per paying subscription-month by plan, Nov 2025-Oct 2026; R3 share of each plan's counted hours reported only at licence renewal; R4 each plan's spring 2024 sign-ups: 24-month paying months and net revenue per sign-up; R5 each plan's 24-month contribution per spring 2027 sign-up; R6 the 2027 remuneration bill; R7 the lead plan
one_fact_test: the licence server's renewals carry the positions of titles played from downloads; moves the careful route from Onbeperkt to Standaard and rescues R6 alone, 1 of 6

lineage.driver: A unit's chance of reaching a milestone is set largely by whether the provider it is attached to keeps operating, providers stop at a rate that peaks a few months into their own tenure, and the forward group was attached almost wholly to providers in their first months, so an exit curve by the unit's own tenure, which validates on closed groups, overstates how many reach the milestone.
lineage.stump: A competent solver projects the autumn campaign's members on the platform's paid-retention curve by membership month, validated on the spring 2025 campaign and last autumn's joiners, and files about EUR 725 per twelfth-month member, inside the EUR 800 bar, and books the re-run; the step that lands it there is projecting each member on their own tenure when the member's cancellation rides on their tutor, and the autumn members' tutors are about to cross the months in which new tutors stop teaching.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-10: the platform's holistic audit failed the uploaded cut on determinism; repaired (judge DETERMINISTIC APPROVE) but the uploaded run's own methods land the repaired commitment (66.5 of 93 graded weight), the single-total risk: one cut of one total cannot be both forced and hard
lineage.driver: A forward total is the sum of several flows each set by its own mechanism (a step change still applying unit by unit at each unit's anniversary, a one-off shock whose excess exit rate has decayed on a cohort whose exits also run with the calendar, a size adjustment at each anniversary set by how much of its capacity each unit uses on a book whose capacity per user has drifted, a pipeline whose conversion falls with each item's age, and exits that arrive together within groups), so every trailing extrapolation and the recent pooled rates overstate the forward total, and the committed figure is the largest step a filed band, carrying the estimates' own sampling error and nothing else, meets at a stated chance.
lineage.stump: A careful but hurried analyst rebuilds the October 2026 ARR correctly, then applies the mean realised uplift to the contracts still to reprice, pools renewal exit and seat-cut rates without utilisation, first renewals or group exits, carries the Team plan's last three months' exit rates, values the open pipeline at the CRM's stage probabilities and draws accounts independently for the band, and files a commitment above the draft, clearing it, when large contracts negotiate the rise down, seat cuts and exits follow utilisation on a book sold more seats per user each year, the autumn is the Team plan's cancellation peak and the January excess has faded, old open deals rarely close and parent groups leave together, so the commitment sits below the draft; and a ten-minute trailing extrapolation clears the draft by a wide margin because the trailing year carries the price rise and the padded seats as if they recurred.
